A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CONSIGN with matching authors, method, and experimental framework. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation experiments on three medical datasets and two COCO subsets, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative samples, calibration values, and computational timings.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional parameter comparisons and qualitative diagnostics in Appendices E and F.

M1.justification: Section 2.3.1 adds an explicit maximum-λ stopping and failure-notification rule to the reported calibration procedure. The SVD construction, prediction sets, losses, sampling procedure, and optimization steps remain unchanged; the cutoff is described in prose without updating Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use M&Ms-2, MS-CMR19, LIDC, COCO-animals, and COCO-vehicles with the same segmentation tasks and represented data. Additional parameter settings and small-region illustrations do not introduce a distinct dataset, population, or input environment.

E2.justification: RAPS and Liu et al.'s SACP remain the evaluated comparators in corresponding experiments and the additional parameter comparisons. The changed SACP neighborhood weight is an experimental-setting revision; newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D changes SACP's reported neighborhood weight from 0.1 for main experiments and 0.4 for appendix experiments to 0.3. Appendix E adds two further (α, β) settings per dataset. Section 3.2 and Appendix C also correct the Chao metric's base count from total draws to distinct samples. Dataset splits, models, and training budgets remain unchanged; these reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E substantially expands sensitivity evidence for confidence and accuracy choices across all five datasets and three metrics. New Appendix F adds targeted diagnostics of uncertainty in small regions (Figure 16) and the relationship between model samples and SVD components (Figure 17). These extend the earlier parameter comparisons and general qualitative examples with additional validation questions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five random calibration/test splits, per-fold calibration values, and ±1 standard-deviation error bars. However, the reported Chao statistical estimator is corrected to use the number of distinct samples, including its bias-corrected form in Appendix C. No additional repetition or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 and six new quantitative plots add results for two further (α, β) settings per dataset, alongside new qualitative diagnostics. Existing CONSIGN and RAPS table entries are retained, while six existing medical-dataset rows for SACP change. For example, Table 5's M&Ms-2 entry at α=0.1, β=0.9, fold 1 changes from 0.630 to 0.580, accompanying the revised SACP setting. The original plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: The Chao estimator's mathematical definition changes from adding total sample count S to adding distinct-sample count S1. Sections 2.2–2.3.1 also qualify the earlier assertion that truncated PCA always permits ground-truth inclusion by acknowledging pathological failures. Lemma 1 and its Appendix A proof remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: spatially informed conformal segmentation sets, statistical coverage guarantees, compatibility with models producing sample predictions, and tighter, more coherent predictions than the evaluated baselines. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds targeted qualifications about pathological nontermination, explains the heuristic and variance-weighted coefficient bounds, discusses dependence on pretrained sample quality and choices of α and β, and explains why pixel-wise samples can look unrealistic. The existing exchangeability, distribution-shift, and computational-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a reproducibility statement and a CONSIGN code-repository link absent from v2. It also documents the practical maximum-λ cutoff and revises the reported SACP weight. Existing dataset and pretrained-model access information, training details, hardware specifications, and runtime Table 2 are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Blot et al. (2025) on group-conditional conformal risk control to the introduction and cites Kingma and Ba for the already-used Adam optimizer. Earlier references and the central positioning relative to spatial UQ and pixel-wise conformal prediction remain.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local edits clarify confidence and accuracy terminology, rename sEC from Sampled Empirical Coverage to Sample-based Estimated Coverage, and expand explanations. A termination subsection, Appendix F, reproducibility statement, and LLM declaration supplement the existing structure.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR layout, expands and redistributes Tables 3–5, and adds six quantitative plots and two diagnostic figures. All nine original figure graphics are retained; v2 Figures 7, 8, and 9 become v3 Figures 12, 9, and 15. Figure 1's caption is expanded, and existing displays move within the reformatted document.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision by correcting the Chao formula and qualifying the overly broad truncated-PCA coverage statement. Additional sensitivity results, small-region examples, component visualizations, and a code pointer improve scrutiny and understanding. These are bounded gains around a retained method and theorem. The unchanged original plots are not reconciled with the revised reported SACP weight, leaving some experimental traceability unclear.
